title: Three trips to the Coast and Julia's reluctance to leave Kansas City
summary: Goodwin believes the pair could have been millionaires, but Julia loved home; agent Johnny Tomino is mentioned.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: You know, I was just looking at some Jay McShann of these W McShann here. Crook, do you want to say something?
Yes. I remember -- I don't remember how many times that Lovett and Julia went to the Coast and made records.

Three different times and I think what I was hoping, I was hoping they would continue on away from Kansas City when they had a chance to be -- I think if they had continued on -- which was no fault of Baby Lovett's, himself, I think that they would have both ended up being millionaires. I think they were just that great because when they would go away on these -- to make records and they were playing different places, well these agents would come to them and they just had their future mapped out for them and the money was there, you know. They could practically name their price or what they wanted to travel and I think it more or less was Julia was a home girl and she just loved Kansas City and she just never did care too much about leaving and staying away from Kansas City.
Well Crook, you refer to her agent.
Johnny Tomino, well he's still around. Well, no he just died didn't he? He's still booking.
Oh, he's retired, but he booked you and Julia out on the Coast?
